subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the public scheduling fields and defaults affects compatibility, persisted job shape, CLI/API behavior, docs, and migrations.

options.title: Design a narrow cron every phase contract
options.body: Add one explicit cron `every` phase/stagger contract with schema, protocol, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve `every` as an anchored fixed interval and rely on heartbeat phase plus cron-expression staggering for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with explicit migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow cron every phase contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit cron `every` phase/stagger contract with schema, protocol, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the cron stagger/product boundary that the remaining decision would change.
